To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coupling noise degradation factor is proportional to the bit-line coupling coefficient, the bit-line resistance, the bit-line capacitance, and inversely proportional to the square of the bit-line length and the square of the clock period.
bit-line coupling and the ground bounce effect have a significant negative impact on the performance of CMOS SRAMs.

the ground bounce effect is the dominant factor in determining the bit-line coupling degradation factor, and the bit-line coupling noise is the dominant factor for determining the ground bounce degradation factor, which are the two main factors that degrade SRAM performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the impact of coupling and ground bounce noises on the performance of SRAMS and the derivation of simple analytical formulas for the coupling noise degradation factor, ground bounce degradation factor, and the noise degradation factor.
the analysis and characterization of the bit-line coupling and the ground bounce effects in SRAM.
the analysis of noise effects on CMOS SRAMS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bit-line coupling and the associated ground bounce noise are very important in SRAM and should be taken into account for the performance optimization of SRAM.
, the ground bounce effect can be neglected in a 90 nm SRAM, but the inter-cell bit-line coupling effect should not be ignored.
the ground bounce effect is the most significant noise source in the SRAM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed formulas are simple and accurate.

the coupling noise degradation factor is a function of the bit-line capacitance and the coupling capacitance, while the ground bounce degradation factor is a linear function of the ground bounce amplitude.
the proposed framework is a very useful tool for the designers to estimate the impact of noises and to predict the performance of SRAMS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coupling noise is more dominant than the ground bounce noise in degrading the performance of SRAMS.
, the ground bounce noise is more detrimental than the bit-line coupling noise in SRAMs.
the ground bounce effect can be more detrimental than the bit-line coupling effect.
